newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto meets husband in jail.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto meets husband in jail.

text.p: Pakistan's deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto met her husband in a jail near Karachi on Thursday and accused President Farooq Leghari of murdering her brother.
"Look, my husband is behind these bars and he is being tortured," a pale-looking Bhutto told reporters as she was brought to see her spouse, Asif Ali Zardari, in Landhi Prison.
"There is no law in the country," she said. "Farooq Leghari is my brother's murderer. He is a worse dictator than (former military ruler General Muhammad) Zia ul-Haq."
Bhutto's estranged brother, Murtaza, died in a hail of police bullets along with seven companions in Karachi on September 20. Police have said his bodyguards fired first.
Murtaza's supporters accuse Zardari of involvement in a conspiracy to kill their leader. He denies the charge.
Leghari's spokesman could not be reached for comment.

The president, once a close political ally of Bhutto, sacked her government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule. The caretaker government he appointed has promised to bring undisclosed charges against Bhutto and Zardari.
Zardari kicked the iron bars and shouted "Jiye (long live) Bhutto" as his wife arrived. "The authorities are mentally torturing me. They want different statements from me."

He said he remained committed to Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) and his country. "I was in the PPP before and I will remain so in the future. I cannot leave Pakistan. I cannot leave my countrymen. I want to remain here in Pakistan," he said.
Zardari sat on a broken wooden chair and spoke through the bars to Bhutto, who sat on a makeshift cement platform.
